en.headline: Jockey Club launches HK$134 million community basketball scheme
en.dek: A five-year programme unveiled on Monday will offer nine-month training in all 18 districts for children aged six to 16, with former NBA player Yao Ming among the guests at the kick-off.
body: The Hong Kong Jockey Club said its Charities Trust has approved more than HK$134 million for a five-year Jockey Club Hoops Connect Community Basketball Programme. A launch ceremony was held on Monday alongside the Philanthropy for Better Cities Forum.

The Club said district youth training will be jointly run by the Boys’ and Girls’ Clubs Association of Hong Kong, the Hong Kong Federation of Youth Groups and the Hong Kong Playground Association, covering all 18 districts with annual nine-month courses for children and young people aged six to 16, particularly those with fewer chances of structured coaching. Coach training will be organised by the Chinese YMCA of Hong Kong.

The scheme is expected to reach more than 4,600 children and young people and to train about 450 coaches, with public activities forecast to draw about 50,000 attendances. Organisers said they would draw on co-operation with the Yao Foundation and on training practice from ALBA Berlin.

Officiating guests included Secretary for Culture, Sports and Tourism Rosanna Law, Jockey Club chief executive Winfried Engelbrecht-Bresges, FIBA secretary general Andreas Zagklis, ALBA Berlin president Axel Schweitzer and Yao Foundation founder Yao Ming. Law said sport also supports physical and mental well-being and social cohesion.

zh.headline: 馬會撥逾1.34億推五年社區籃球計劃
zh.dek: 賽馬會「傳承接力」社區籃球計劃周一啟動，將於18區為6至16歲兒童及青年提供每年九個月訓練，前NBA球星姚明出席典禮。
body: 香港賽馬會表示，慈善信託基金已審批撥捐逾1.34億港元，推行五年期的賽馬會「傳承接力」社區籃球計劃。啟動禮周一與香港國際公益慈善論壇同場舉行。
馬會表示，地區青年訓練由香港小童群益會、香港青年協會及香港遊樂場協會聯合推行，覆蓋全港18區，每年為6至16歲兒童及青年提供為期九個月的有系統訓練，特別針對因經濟或社會因素而較少機會接受正規訓練的年輕人。教練培訓則由香港中華基督教青年會舉辦。
計劃預計惠及逾4,600名兒童及青年，並培訓約450名教練，公眾活動預計吸引約5萬人次參與。主辦單位表示會借助與姚基金的合作，以及德國歐綠保柏林籃球隊的訓練經驗。
主禮嘉賓包括文化體育及旅遊局局長羅淑佩、馬會行政總裁應家柏、國際籃球聯會秘書長Andreas Zagklis、歐綠保柏林籃球隊總裁史偉浩，以及姚基金創辦人姚明。羅淑佩表示，體育除提升運動表現外，亦有助身心健康及促進社會凝聚力。
